subject: Private deployment upgrade: cordon choreography, version-pinning cadence, and rollback rubric
messages:

Subject: Private fleet upgrade window request + network cordon question

Irene —

Thanks for the prep call earlier. Our ops team wants to schedule the June maintenance for the on-prem Redwood private deployment (cluster A). A couple quick asks before we lock a date:

- Can you confirm the recommended maintenance window length for a minor patch (non-breaking config + qf kernels)?
- What's your suggestion for cordoning strategy so we minimize evictions for pinned versions? We run a mix of latency-sensitive endpoints and batch ingest.
- Do you have a shorthand rollback rubric we can follow if the new runtime exhibits token-regression issues?

We're aiming for a low-mid-week window (Tue/Wed) to avoid weekend staffing. Happy to share calendar availability.

Thanks —
Will Price

Subject: Re: Private fleet upgrade window request + network cordon question

Will —

Thanks, appreciate the heads-up. Proposed answers and a draft plan below; attaching the preflight checklist and a short rollback rubric (attached). Please review and confirm gaps.

Summary recommendations:
- Window length: 3 hours for a non-breaking minor runtime/CR patch. That covers drain, staged deploy, short validation (15m), and a 60-minute observation/rollback hold.
- Cordon choreography: stagger node cordons in waves of 10-15% of capacity with KV cache warmup disabled per wave. Start with a canary (single node) in a non-latency-critical rack, validate end-to-end, then proceed 20/20/40/20. This keeps tail latency predictable.
- Version pinning cadence: pin API-facing services to a model/runtime minor patch for 72 hours in a canary cohort; after no regressions, extend pins to 50% for 24 hours, then full. Document the pin with an explicit semantic tag (e.g., runtime-1.4.2-pin-20270617).
- Rollback rubric (high level): revert to last pinned runtime if any of: sustained +5% P95 latency, token-level error rate >0.5% on golden prompts, or service error rate >1% for 15 continuous minutes. We include an automated rollback trigger and a manual approval path.

Operational play (draft):
1) Preflight (24h before): run preflight checks (attached). Provide artifacts to SOC (audit log, drift hash).
2) Canary (T+0): cordon canary node, apply patch, run smoke + golden prompt set (10m). If pass, uncordon and proceed.
3) Wave 1 (T+30m): cordon 15% capacity nodes in rack A, deploy, run load validation (30m).
4) Wave 2 (T+70m): expand to another 20%; run KV warmup with synthetic prefixes.
5) Observation hold (60m): monitor P95/P99, token error rate, tracing.
6) Rollout/Abort: If thresholds hit, run rollback script (attached). If manual abort, run extra validation on failing nodes before reintroducing.

Attachments: redwood_private_preflight-checklist.pdf, rollback-rubric.md, network-drain.sh

Questions for you:
- Can Acme provide a 1-hour maintenance coordinator (on-call) for real-time decisions?
- Which night/day preference between Tue/Wed in your timezone (PST)?

I'll loop Jonas in for low-level cordon details.

—Irene Choi

Short technical notes from the runtime/infrastructure side —

- Drain behavior: use the soft-drain flag for latency endpoints to allow existing token streams to finish; set hard-drain for batch workers. Script example included in network-drain.sh (attached).
- KV cache strategy: disable prefix cache population during the first two waves to avoid cache churn; enable a warmup subtask in wave 3 with conservative rate limits.
- Circuit breakers: ensure the canary process has a fallback route to the last-stable small-quant model variant (runtime-1.4.1-quant) in case of memory pressure. We'll publish mapping in the rollout ticket (JIRA INF-1427).
- Tracing hooks: attach a short golden-prompt trace (trace id sample) to the rollout ticket so we can quickly compare token latencies.

One practical ask: include the precise IP ranges and NAT gateway planned for the cordoned nodes (for firewall rules). We need those to pre-provision temporary routing to the fallback pool.

I'll be on-call during the Wed window and can trigger the automated rollback if thresholds breach.

-Jonas Weber
Director, Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference
